title: Replace legacy token parsers with strict JWT verifier and OpenSSL 3 compatibility shim
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: Over the past years we accumulated several auth token parsing paths: a legacy permissive JWT parser used by some older services, a couple of home-grown OAuth helpers, and a thin SAML XML adapter that relies on an external xmlsec binary. These code paths are inconsistent about strictness (kid verification, alg validation, exp/nbf handling), key discovery and caching, and they tie into a mix of OpenSSL 1.1.x APIs. This has caused intermittent token validation regressions and complicated upgrades to OpenSSL 3.x and FIPS-aware builds.

Goal: Replace the legacy permissive token parsers across runtime services with a single strict JWT verification library and a compatibility shim that adapts OpenSSL 3.x APIs to our internal KMS/PKCS11 integration. Remove dependency on the external xmlsec adapter for signed SAML assertions in favor of our native verification path.

Scope / deliverables:
- Implement a library (internal/jwt/strict) that enforces: algorithm allowlist, explicit kid resolution, JWK set caching + backoff, strict exp/nbf/leeway rules, and aud/iss verification hooks.
- Create an OpenSSL 3 compatibility shim that maps older EVP APIs we call into supported 3.x equivalents and adds optional FIPS-mode switches for Private deployments.
- Migrate three runtime services (auth-proxy, routing-service, eval-ingest) to use the new verifier.
- Replace xmlsec invocation for SAML signed-assertion checks with a hardened native verifier using libxml + our crypto shim.
- Add unit and integration tests, a canary rollout plan, and runtime feature flags to revert to the legacy parser if needed.

Acceptance criteria:
- All standard JWT/OIDC conformance tests pass against the new verifier and test vectors (RS256, ES256, HS256) including malformed token rejection tests.
- No increase in end-to-end auth latency >2ms p50 for validated requests after migration; e2e throughput regression <3% under our benchmark harness.
- OpenSSL library upgrade to 3.x on a staging cluster with shim applied and no missing symbols or runtime errors.
- Observability: token validation metric tags (verifier_version, jwk_cache_hits) added to Console; alert if verifier errors spike >5x baseline during canary.
- Security review completed and signed-off by Security team.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge library and shim behind feature flag; run unit tests and static analysis.
2) Deploy to staging runtime-1.19 cluster and run nightly conformance suite.
3) Canary on 2% traffic for auth-proxy for 72 hours with throttled ramp. Monitor errors and latency.
4) Expand to routing-service and eval-ingest after 72h healthy window.
5) Full rollout and deprecation of legacy parser after two weeks.

Risks & mitigations:
- JWK discovery latency: implement local warming and cache jitter; fall back to legacy path only if verification fails due to fetch timeouts and feature flag allows it.
- Signature algorithm mismatches from third-party integrations: add temporary opt-in allowlist per-customer to avoid breaking enterprise customers; engage account owners.
- OpenSSL symbol incompatibilities: run binary-level smoke tests and stage shim in a separate control-plane container to validate KMS integration before pushing to runtime.

Notes: This is a security-sensitive change; coordinate with SRE for rollback playbooks and with Security for threat modelling and a short pen-test window before full rollout.
